title: Andhra University Takes Centenary to US Alumni, Houston MoU Discussed
excerpt: Vice-Chancellor G.P. Raja Sekhar's delegation drew 200 alumni in Sugar Land, discussed a University of Houston MoU, and heads to Penn State and New Jersey.
body:
• An Andhra University delegation led by Vice-Chancellor G.P. Raja Sekhar is touring the United States for the university's centenary outreach, with a final alumni meeting at Fords, New Jersey, on Saturday, October 17.
  • About 200 alumni attended the first celebration at Sugar Land, Texas, on October 10, where 50 alumni were felicitated.
  • The delegation discussed a proposed MoU with the University of Houston covering superconductivity, energy security, meteorology and oceanography, advanced materials and an AI Systems Centre of Excellence.
  • For US-based alumni: the New Jersey gathering will discuss artificial intelligence in higher education and how alumni contributions can be organised — mentoring, partnerships and endowments are the university's stated asks.

Andhra University has taken its centenary celebrations to its alumni in the United States. A delegation led by Vice-Chancellor G.P. Raja Sekhar has begun a series of engagements in the US as part of the university's centenary outreach, and the tour combines alumni celebrations with talks on a proposed academic partnership with the University of Houston, according to The Hindu report republished by Conven.org.

Sugar Land Opens the Tour

The Andhra University Alumni Association of North America organised the first celebration at Sugar Land, Texas, on October 10. About 200 alumni attended and 50 were felicitated, with Raja Sekhar as chief guest. S. Paul Douglas, Dean of International Affairs, and Prashant Kumar Sona, Consul at the Consulate General of India in Houston, were guests of honour.

The Vice-Chancellor urged alumni to support mentoring, institutional partnerships and endowments. Asked about accountability for donations, he said a draft endowment policy would be released soon. Participants also discussed compliance with Indian rules on foreign contributions and the possibility of US tax-exempt status for donations — the two practical questions that determine whether diaspora giving can move from goodwill to a working channel.

The Houston MoU on the Table

Raja Sekhar and Douglas met University of Houston President Renu Khator and Ramanan Krishnamoorti, Vice-President for Energy and Innovation, to discuss a proposed Memorandum of Understanding. The priority areas named were superconductivity, energy security, meteorology and oceanography, advanced materials, and an AI Systems Centre of Excellence with high-performance computing and 5G technologies. The delegation also met D.C. Manjunath, Consul General of India in Houston, to discuss prioritising MoUs with American universities.

The Houston discussion is a proposal at this stage, not a signed agreement. Its subject list is telling: it pairs Andhra University's coastal strengths — meteorology and oceanography for a university in Visakhapatnam on the Bay of Bengal — with Houston's energy base and a shared interest in advanced computing.

A Centenary Year of Partnerships

The US tour follows the university's main centenary celebrations in Visakhapatnam, where, as India Education Diary reported, three MoUs were exchanged between Andhra University and the University of Florida, Oxmiq Labs Inc. in the US, and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, in the presence of Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan. Distinguished Alumni Awards at that event went to figures including former Vice-President M. Venkaiah Naidu and GMR Group founder Grandhi Mallikarjuna Rao. Founded in 1926, the university is using its hundredth year to convert a large overseas alumni base into formal research and mentoring ties.

What Happens Next on the Tour

The delegation left for Penn State University on Thursday, with a meeting there on Friday. The final meeting is scheduled at Fords, New Jersey, on Saturday, October 17, and will include discussions on artificial intelligence in higher education and on organising alumni contributions. For alumni in the New York-New Jersey area, that session is the remaining open stop on this tour — and, given the Sugar Land agenda, the place where questions about the draft endowment policy and donation routes can be put directly to the Vice-Chancellor's team.
